paragraphs.text: Bandaranaike International Airport, the main of Sri Lanka's five international airports, has three passenger terminals. Terminal 1, opened in 1967, is the largest and oldest; all arrivals and departures take place through its gates, which are reached from a single passenger concourse.
After the security checks, gates 6 to 14 are on the upper floor and the remaining gates on the lower floor. Terminal 3, opened in November 2012, serves domestic flights.

Terminal 2 was scheduled to begin construction in April 2017 and be completed in 2020, with eight gates (two able to take the Airbus A380), five floors, a car park and a hotel. Plans were set back by the COVID-19 pandemic and the economic crisis; in May 2025 the airport's chairman told the Daily Mirror that bids had been invited from two Japanese companies.

Since June 2025 the Route 187 luxury air-conditioned bus has run between the airport and Colombo Fort on the Colombo–Katunayake Expressway, avoiding city traffic. It boards at the Departure Terminal Outer Porch and runs 24 hours a day.
Terminal 1 has two main passenger lounges, Serendib and Palm Spirit.
In August 2022 the airport opened the Golden Route arrival lounge for premium passengers, who can use it to complete immigration, emigration and customs checks without queuing.

faqs.q: Is there a bus from Colombo airport to the city?
faqs.a: Yes. Since June 2025 the Route 187 luxury air-conditioned bus has run 24 hours a day between the airport and Colombo Fort on the expressway, boarding at the Departure Terminal Outer Porch.

faqs.q: Which terminal do international flights use at Colombo airport?
faqs.a: Terminal 1. Terminal 3 serves domestic flights, and Terminal 2 had not yet been built as of May 2025.
